title: Sharp Bounds on Harm among Stayers under Multilayer Response-Type Restrictions

proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved sharp harmed-stayer programs with an exact decoder for arbitrary finite linear response-type restrictions, then proved the Cartesian prism, O(|X|L) endpoints, and iff harm certificate under KMV Strong Monotonicity. The identification mathematics survived maximality and correctness review, but the promised numerical-delta validity result at hinge ties and structural zeros was not proved. Reaching field tier would require that new inference theorem plus meaningful implementation or empirical validation, so the sound result was banked at subfield tier.
tldr: Conditional random assignment identifies the arm-specific layer--outcome margins but not the joint response type, same-positive-layer stayer mass, or harm among those stayers. For any finite set of KMV linear response-type restrictions \(\mathcal R_T\), an expanded-state flow polytope gives sharp conditional harm-fraction endpoints as two explicit Charnes--Cooper linear programs, with an exact decoder and a finite-strata aggregate obtained by weighting numerator and denominator by \(P(X=x)\). KMV Remark 2(i) already includes \(D_1\ge D_0\) as Strong Monotonicity; the genuine closed-form contribution is the binary-harm collapse in that submodel: the stayer diagonal is a Cartesian box, the joint stayer--harm region is an exact prism, and its ratio contracts to sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints with an observable iff certificate for unavoidable harm. A protocol-controlled retain-or-upgrade tier design is one credibility example, not the source or claimed novelty of Strong Monotonicity.
gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already supplies sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds under multilayer selection. Their Assumption 2 imposes only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits both directions among positive layers, so it neither states nor supports ordered-layer monotonicity. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele provide the closest multi-tier harm comparison: their sharp bounds concern movement across tiers of ordered outcome categories. Binary harm results handle one observed stratum or fully observed arm marginals. No inspected result characterizes harm within latent same-layer stayers jointly with an unidentified sum of same-tier stayer masses under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers.
fill: Three identification theorems establish the diagonal box, the exact joint stayer--harm prism, and sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints for protocol-assigned tiers. The unavoidable-harm corollary and exact rational two-layer attainment witness make the identification result directly auditable. Generic numerical-delta and confidence-set image operations remain ordinary implementation prose.
